pageCache.pageTitle: Appeal timetable 2026 - Epsom and Ewell High School
pageCache.text:
Appeal timetable 2026
Appeals for September 2026 entry resulting from year of entry or transfer applications.
Appeals to be heard by
16 June 2026 (40 school days)
17 July 2026 (40 school days)
Please note: Appeals will not start being heard until after the relevant closing date has passed.
Appeals lodged after these dates will be heard within 40 school days of the appeal deadline or 30 school days of being lodged, whichever is the later date.
Appeals are not heard in school holidays, which will vary depending on the school.
Appellants will be sent notification of their appeal hearing at least 10 clear school days in advance of the hearing. Appellants will be sent a copy of the school's case normally a week in advance of the hearing.
Appellants must ensure that any further evidence not included with their initial appeal is received by the stated deadline, which will be clearly highlighted in the appeal hearing notification letter. Any additional evidence or information received after this date might not be considered at the appeal hearing.
In-year or immediate entry appeals
Appeals resulting from in year admission applications will be heard within 30 school days of the appeal being lodged.

pageCache.pageTitle: Admissions & open events - Epsom and Ewell High School
pageCache.text:
Admissions & open events
We know that moving from primary to secondary school is a significant step for students and their families.
The best way to understand life at Epsom & Ewell High School is to see it for yourself. We warmly invite prospective students and parents to visit, explore our classrooms and facilities, meet our staff and students, and get a real sense of our school community.
Our team is always happy to answer questions and provide guidance to help make the transition as smooth as possible.
For information on how to apply, including Surrey’s online application form and key dates, please see below.
Surrey School admissions - apply for your school place here
Contact Mrs Sara Dibley (Admissions Officer) with any queries
Admissions Arrangements 2027-28
Admissions Arrangements 2026-27
Admissions Arrangements 2025-26
EEHS School Admissions Consultation (September 2027)
In-year admissions - how to apply for a place if you are moving during the school year
Appeal timetable 2026
Sixth Form Admissions
Summary of the application process
There are six steps in the application process.
Step 1: Research and choose schools to apply for
You research and choose the schools that you want to apply for. You can apply for up to six schools. You should also check if your child will be eligible for free home to school transport to your chosen schools. If your child is not eligible for free home to school transport it will be your responsibility as a parent to get your child to and from school.
You should try to do this as early as possible.
Step 2: Complete the application form
You complete the application form and return it to the local authority where you live. You submit supporting documents with your application form if you are applying under exceptional social or medical criteria.
Some schools also ask for a supplementary form in addition to the application form.
Step 3: Applications are assessed
Applications are ranked according to each school's criteria. Surrey CC then determine the best offer that can be made based on the order of preferences on your application form.
Step 4: Surrey CC offer you a place
Surrey CC will tell you the outcome of your application.
Step 5: You accept or decline the place
You must accept or decline the place.
Step 6: If you don't get a place at your preferred school
If you are unhappy with the school place that has been offered, you can appeal. For Surrey schools you must do this by the dates shown in the appeals timetable or the dates set out against each school in Surrey's directory of Surrey schools.
You can also add your child's name to the waiting list for your preferred school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our curriculum - Epsom and Ewell High School
pageCache.text:
Our curriculum
At Epsom & Ewell High School, students benefit from an ambitious curriculum from key stage 3 through to key stage 5, giving them the opportunity to continue their learning with us into their post-16 studies.
Across the school we offer more than 30 subjects, taught by specialist staff with strong subject expertise, ensuring that every student is challenged to achieve their absolute best. Our curriculum is designed to stretch and inspire students, supporting them to ROAR in their learning - developing resilience when tackling challenging ideas, remaining open-minded when exploring different perspectives, aspiring to achieve their very best, and reflecting on their progress to continually improve.
Beyond the classroom, students are supported through a range of additional opportunities, including a homework club that runs throughout the week to provide guidance and support outside of core lessons. All students are encouraged to take part in at least one extra-curricular club each term and can engage with programmes such as the Duke of Edinburgh’s Award and The Brilliant Club. Highlights include our annual school production, extensive sporting programme, and house competitions, all of which foster teamwork, confidence, and a strong sense of community.
Students learn in a modern, well-equipped environment, with large classrooms, dedicated arts and performance spaces, and excellent sporting facilities. These spaces provide the practical and creative resources students need to succeed, supporting learning, enrichment, and personal development across every stage of the curriculum.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND - Epsom and Ewell High School
pageCache.text:
SEND
At EEHS we expect all students to study a broad and balanced curriculum and students with SEND are no exception to this.
We believe offering a broad and balanced curriculum, along with additional support where necessary, is the route to success for all students. There is strong evidence that studying a modern foreign language is extremely beneficial to students with SEND. Studying a language can:
Improve understanding of language constructs
Improve articulation
Develop social skills
Develop cultural awareness
Improve memory
Build self-esteem
Specialist Resourced Provision for Deaf Children
At Epsom and Ewell High School we have a specialist resourced provision which strives to individualise our student support, enabling a successful and challenging mainstream education for our deaf students.

pageCache.pageTitle: Governors - Epsom and Ewell High School
pageCache.text:
Governors
Governors play an important role in the life of our school. They take a long-term strategic view of the way in which the school is developing. Their main function is to ensure that the school improves so that the highest standards possible are achieved in all aspects of school life.
In many ways, a governing committee is like a board of directors of a company: they make decisions about standards, policies, funding and recruitment of senior staff. The headteacher and the staff are responsible for the day-to-day running of the school. They work hard to implement the School Improvement Plan. It is the responsibility of the governors to challenge and support the school in its ways of achieving the best for students.
The Local Governing Committee oversees the strategic direction of the school.
Governors' duties include:
promoting high standards
setting targets for pupil achievement
managing the school's budget

pageCache.pageTitle: Our sporting edge - Epsom and Ewell High School
pageCache.text:
Our sporting edge
At Epsom & Ewell, students benefit from extensive grounds and outstanding sporting facilities that are among the strongest in Surrey, providing excellent opportunities for participation, training and competition.
A £12 million investment has created a modern, high-quality sporting environment where students can excel in sport, fitness and physical education, reinforcing the school’s long-standing commitment to providing outstanding facilities and opportunities. At the centre of the campus are multiple indoor sports halls built to Sport England standards, designed to support a wide range of curriculum and extra-curricular activities including badminton, basketball, volleyball and netball. These versatile spaces ensure students have access to professional-level indoor training environments throughout the school day.
The redevelopment also delivered exceptional outdoor facilities, including a full-size 3G all-weather pitch, professional-grade grass football pitches, a purpose-built athletics track, and high-quality tennis and hockey areas. Together, these facilities enable students to train, compete and develop their skills in a safe, high-performance environment that supports both team and individual sports.
Complementing the sports programme is the gym and studio space, alongside modern dance and performing arts studios. These provide high-quality indoor training and activity spaces, with modern equipment, fitness rooms and wellbeing areas tailored to student use, supporting physical development and promoting healthy, active lifestyles across all year groups.
These facilities underpin a full extra-curricular sports programme that is open to all students. Every student is actively encouraged to take part in at least one activity each week, helping them to stay active, develop teamwork and leadership skills, and enjoy the many benefits of being part of a thriving sporting community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our wellbeing - Epsom and Ewell High School
pageCache.text:
Our wellbeing
At Epsom & Ewell, we believe that academic success and wellbeing go hand in hand. Our aim is to ensure that every student is supported to achieve the very best results while developing the confidence, resilience and independence to pursue ambitious futures and succeed in whatever path they choose.
Our approach focuses on the whole child. Alongside high-quality teaching and a challenging curriculum, students are supported to develop the habits, attitudes and self-belief that underpin successful learning.
Dedicated time within the timetable encourages students to reflect on the kind of learners they want to be, to approach challenges positively and to develop strategies that help them persevere when learning becomes demanding. By nurturing wellbeing alongside academic ambition, we create an environment where students feel supported to take intellectual risks, learn from setbacks and continually improve. This helps them build resilience, strong relationships and a sense of responsibility for their own progress.
As a result, students leave Epsom & Ewell not only with strong academic outcomes, but also with the confidence, character and determination needed to succeed in the next stage of their education and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reading - Epsom and Ewell High School
pageCache.text:
Reading
Once you learn to read, you will be forever free.
- Attributed to Frederick Douglass
At Epsom and Ewell High School, we recognise that supporting children to become capable and engaged readers plays an important role in their future success. Reading empowers; it facilitates education and employment, and it enriches one’s personal life and growth.
We use diagnostic tests to accurately identify gaps in students’ reading knowledge and use this to provide a bespoke accelerated pathway for those children who are pre-key stage readers through a research-based reading intervention.
Reading across the curriculum
Literacy is key to learning across all subjects in secondary school and a strong predictor of outcomes in later life.
One of our whole school priorities is 'disciplinary literacy'; an approach to improving literacy across the curriculum that emphasises the importance of subject specific support. We are committed to ensuring our students are learning how to read, write and communicate effectively in each of their subject areas.
Supporting your child with reading
We understand that the digital environment in which today's students are immersed can easily distract them from reading. As parents, you play a crucial role in helping them establish healthy habits. For instance, encourage them to read for a minimum of 20 minutes per day, and prioritise reading before engaging with screens. Engaging your child in discussions about their reading to foster comprehension and interest is also helpful.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our curriculum - Epsom and Ewell High School
pageCache.text:
Our curriculum
At Epsom & Ewell High School, students benefit from an ambitious curriculum from key stage 3 through to key stage 5, giving them the opportunity to continue their learning with us into their post-16 studies.
Across the school we offer more than 30 subjects, taught by specialist staff with strong subject expertise, ensuring that every student is challenged to achieve their absolute best. Our curriculum is designed to stretch and inspire students, supporting them to ROAR in their learning - developing resilience when tackling challenging ideas, remaining open-minded when exploring different perspectives, aspiring to achieve their very best, and reflecting on their progress to continually improve.
Beyond the classroom, students are supported through a range of additional opportunities, including a homework club that runs throughout the week to provide guidance and support outside of core lessons. All students are encouraged to take part in at least one extra-curricular club each term and can engage with programmes such as the Duke of Edinburgh’s Award and The Brilliant Club. Highlights include our annual school production, extensive sporting programme, and house competitions, all of which foster teamwork, confidence, and a strong sense of community.
Students learn in a modern, well-equipped environment, with large classrooms, dedicated arts and performance spaces, and excellent sporting facilities. These spaces provide the practical and creative resources students need to succeed, supporting learning, enrichment, and personal development across every stage of the curriculum.
